title: Comparing two builds

milestone.title: Ground Rules, Tools and the PE Format

description:
A hex editor's compare view is one of the most used tools in reversing: build your program twice with one small change and compare the files to see exactly which bytes the change touched. Write its core:

```cpp
struct Change { std::size_t offset; std::size_t length; };

std::vector<Change> diffBytes(const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& before, const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& after);
std::string describe(const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& before, const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& after, Change c);
```

- **diffBytes** returns the runs of consecutive differing bytes, in order. If one file is longer, everything past the end of the shorter one counts as different (joined to a run that reaches the end of the shorter one).
- **describe** formats one change as `0xOFFSET: BEFORE -> AFTER`: the offset in uppercase hex without padding, then the bytes of each side as two uppercase hex digits separated by spaces. A byte position that a side does not have is shown as `--`.

```text
0x1A: 74 05 -> EB 05
0x40: -- -- -> 90 C3
```
hints: Treat "past the end of one side" as "different" in a single helper, then the main loop is just: skip equal bytes, then measure a run of different ones.
